# Preface {.unnumbered}

STEP, formally ISO 10303, is the international standard for representing and exchanging product data.
Almost every mechanical CAD system can read and write it, and a large share of the world's engineering data crosses company boundaries as `.stp` files.
Yet the standard itself is vast, expensive, and written for implementers rather than for the people who use it day to day.

This book is an attempt to fill that gap.
It explains what a STEP file actually contains, how it is structured, what the standard does and does not guarantee, and how to work with it in practice.

## Who this book is for {.unnumbered}

- Engineers and designers who exchange CAD data and want to understand what happens to it.
- Software developers writing importers, exporters, or tooling for STEP data.
- Students and researchers who need an approachable introduction before reading the standard itself.

No prior knowledge of ISO 10303 is assumed.
Familiarity with 3D CAD concepts such as solids, faces, and assemblies will help.

## How the book is organized {.unnumbered}

**Part I, Foundations**, introduces the standard and dissects a real STEP file line by line.
**Part II, The Standard**, covers the EXPRESS modelling language and the Application Protocols that define which entities may appear in a file.
The appendices collect a glossary and reference material.

## Conventions {.unnumbered}

Entity names from the standard are written in `SMALL_CAPS_WITH_UNDERSCORES`, exactly as they appear in a Part 21 file.
Listings that show file contents are complete and can be saved and opened in a CAD system unless stated otherwise.

## Source and contributions {.unnumbered}

This book is open source.
The text is written in Quarto Markdown and lives at <https://github.com/jchultarsky/step-book>.
Corrections and contributions are welcome; see the contributing guide in the repository.
